out_items.name: Food separated and protected

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal Foods Different Types
violations.observation: Different types of raw animal foods stored in such a manner that may cause cross contamination as follows: raw chicken was stored over raw beef in the walk-in refrigerator.
violations.corrective_action: Raw animal foods shall be sorted by their 'type' and cooking temperatures while in storage inside a refrigerator or freezer. For example, if using ONE shelving unit for storage of ONLY raw foods, the foods shall be sorted in this manner: 1) raw poultry (chicken, turkey, or duck) shall be stored on the BOTTOM shelf (165F cook temperature), 2) raw ground beef and ground pork shall be stored on the shelf above poultry (155F cook temperature), and 3) raw pork (chops, ribs), seafood, and shell eggs shall be stored on the top shelf above beef (145F cook temperature). The PIC moved the raw foods to appropriate storage locations during the inspection to correct.

out_items.name: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used

violations.title: Separation of Poison/Toxic Materials
violations.observation: Observed that poisonous and toxic materials are not properly stored to prevent the contamination of food, equipment, utensils, linens or single service items. Potatoes were stored on the chemical storage shelf.
violations.corrective_action: All poisonous and toxic materials shall be stored to prevent contamination of food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single service items by separating the poisonous and toxic materials by spacing or partitioning. The PIC moved the potatoes during the inspection to correct.

violations.title: Common Name, Working Containers
violations.observation: Working containers of poisonous and toxic materials are not properly labeled with a common name. There was an unlabeled spray bottle of cleaning chemical in the kitchen
violations.corrective_action: Label all working containers of poisonous and toxic materials, including cleaners and sanitizers, with a common name to prevent the dangerous misuse of these materials. The PIC labeled the spray bottle during the inspection to correct.

out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.title: Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, Durable/Smooth Materials
violations.observation: The nonfood-contact surface of the following equipment is not corrosion resistant, nonabsorbent, and/or smooth: folded cardboard boxes were being used to line shelving and flooring in the kitchen. The cardboard is visibly soiled with food debris and grease.
violations.corrective_action: Folded cardboard boxes are not an approved material for lining shelving in a food establishment. Remove the cardboard boxes and discontinue using folded cardboard boxes to line shelving. Instead, keep the shelving clean on a frequent basis. RCL Raouche Cafe Liban LLC (Inspection Date: 08/11/2026) Page 2 of 3

out_items.name: Toilet facilities properly constructed, supplied, and cleaned

violations.title: Toilet Rooms Enclosed
violations.observation: The door to the bathroom located in the kitchen was propped open, not self-closing, and there were odors emitting from the bathroom. Toilet room door is not provided with a self-closing door.
violations.corrective_action: Provide a self-closing hinge or closing mechanism for the toilet room door. Correct as soon as possible or before the next routine inspection not to exceed 6 moths.

out_items.name: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean

violations.title: Physical Facilities, Cleaning Frequency
violations.observation: Observed that the kitchen floor was very soiled and in need of cleaning. Also observed the ceiling panels were visibly soiled and need of cleaning.
violations.corrective_action: Clean the physical facilities at a frequency necessary to ensure the protection and safe preparation of food. The PIC stated the floor is cleaned frequently and that it is stained. If the floor can no longer be cleaned due to its condition, it may need to be replaced. Instead of replacing, it is recommended that the floor be cleaned more frequently. If the ceiling panels can’t be cleaned, they need to be replaced. Correct as soon as possible or before the next routine inspection, not to exceed 6 months.

violations.title: Physical Facilities, Maintain Good Repair
violations.observation: Observed one light fixture in the kitchen was not working, lightbulbs and the light shield was missing. There are also several light bulbs not working in the remaining kitchen lights. The light fixtures are 4-bulb fixtures; all light bulbs must be working to provide sufficient lighting.
violations.corrective_action: Repair the physical facilities. Poor repair and maintenance compromises the functionality of the physical facilities. The PIC stated the light fixture broke yesterday and it will be repaired soon. Correct as soon as possible or before the next routine inspection, not to exceed 6 months.

out_items.name: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible

violations.title: Paper Towels Provided
violations.observation: Observed that paper towels were not provided at each handwashing sink. There were no paper towels at the main handwashing sink in the kitchen.
violations.corrective_action: Provide paper towels at each hand sink to allow employees to properly dry their hands after handwashing. The PIC refilled the paper towel dispenser during the inspection. CDI.

out_items.name: Food separated and protected

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal Foods Different Types
violations.observation: Different types of raw animal foods stored in such a manner that may cause cross contamination as follows: raw chicken was stored over raw beef in the walker refrigerator. Also raw ground beef was stored over raw whole beef in the walk-in refrigerator.
violations.corrective_action: Raw animal foods shall be sorted by their 'type' and cooking temperatures while in storage inside a refrigerator or freezer. For example, if using ONE shelving unit for storage of ONLY raw foods, the foods shall be sorted in this manner: 1) raw poultry (chicken, turkey, or duck) shall be stored on the BOTTOM shelf (165F cook temperature), 2) raw ground beef and ground pork shall be stored on the shelf above poultry (155F cook temperature), and 3) raw pork (chops, ribs), seafood, and shell eggs shall be stored on the top shelf above beef (145F cook temperature). The EHS explained the proper way to store raw foods to prevent contamination. The pic rearranged the raw foods during the inspection. CDI.

out_items.name: Proper cooling time and temperature

violations.title: Cooling from 135F to 70F, No More than 2 Hours
violations.observation: The following cooked time/temperature control for safety food(s) are not being adequately cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours. There were two large containers of cooked beef with pie nuts sitting on the table in the kitchen for more than two hours that were 85° and 91° respectively the kitchen staff is not tracking cooling temperatures, so it was not possible to tell when cooling started.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety foods shall be cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours to prevent the growth of harmful bacteria. Foods that have been temperature abused are to be discarded. The pic was told if the food had been between 135 degrees and 70 degrees for more than two hours that the food had to be discarded. He said he wasn’t sure when the food hit 135°. The food was discarded. CDI.

out_items.name: Proper cold holding temperatures

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: grape leaves prepared that day and in the walk-in were 78°F and had been cooling for almost 4 hours
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. The PIC placed the grape leaves in the freezer to cool down more quickly.

out_items.name: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used

violations.title: Common Name, Working Containers
violations.observation: Working containers of poisonous and toxic materials are not properly labeled with a common name. There were two spray bottles of table cleaner in the dining area, which were not labeled.
violations.corrective_action: Label all working containers of poisonous and toxic materials, including cleaners and sanitizers, with a common name to prevent the dangerous misuse of these materials. The bottles were labeled during the inspection. CDI. RCL Raouche Cafe Liban LLC (Inspection Date: 02/12/2026) Page 2 of 4

out_items.name: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control

violations.title: Methods to Facilitate Proper Cooling
violations.observation: The following methods used for cooling were not adequate to facilitate proper cooling: observed large quantities of ground beef and soup being cooled on the counter covered and not in reduced portions. The beef was cooked at 9:30 and was 85° but it was unknown at what time the cooling started because the establishment is not tracking cooling times. They were also foods that were prepped from ambient temperature that were not cold enough in the walk-in. This included stuffed grape leaves which were 78° and had been cooling for four hours.
violations.corrective_action: Cooling hot foods shall be accomplished as follows: 1) placing the food in shallow pans; 2) separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; 3) using rapid cooling equipment; 4) stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; 5) using containers that facilitate heat transfer; 6) adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Food containers placed in cooling and cold equipment to cool shall be: 1) arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the containers walls, and 2) loosely covered or uncovered as long as protected from contamination to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food. The EHS explained how foods need to be cooled properly to the PIC. The PIC said he would work on reducing the amount of food being cooled so that it will cool more quickly. CDI.

out_items.name: Approved thawing methods used

violations.title: Proper thawing methods used for TCS Foods
violations.observation: Observed the following food thawing using an improper method: cooked ground beef with pine nuts was being thawed at room temperature. Also containers of frozen soup were being thawed at room temperature under the hood.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be thawed using one of the following methods: 1) under refrigeration that maintains the food temperature at 41F or less, 2) completely submerged under running water at a water temperature of 70F or below with a sufficient velocity to agitate and float off loose particles of food as long as held for period of time at a temperature of 41F or less, or 3) as part of a cooking process if the food is cooked as specified by Law or thawed in a microwave oven and immediately transferred to a conventional cooking process. The EHS discussed this with the PIC. CDI.

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Food Storage 6 inches above Floor
violations.observation: Food stored on the floor and/or food stored less than 6 inches off the floor. Observed cases of food and equipment stored on the floor in several areas of the establishment.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food at least 6 inches off the floor on approved shelving units or dunnage racks. Milk crates, soda crates, or bread racks are not suitable for food storage. All food must be stored at at least 6 inches out the floor at all times, unless just received correct as soon as possible or before the next routine inspection.

out_items.name: Personal cleanliness

violations.title: Hair Restraints
violations.observation: Employees observed working in the food service area without proper hair restraints. One of the food handlers was not wearing a hair restraint while working with foods.
violations.corrective_action: Food employees shall wear hair restraints such as hats, visors, hair nets or beard nets to effectively keep their hair from contacting exposed food, clean equipment, utensils, linens, and unwrapped single-service items. This section does not apply to food employees such as counter staff who ONLY serve beverages and wrapped or packaged foods, hostesses, and wait staff. The food handler donned a hairnet during the inspection. CDI.

out_items.name: Non-food contact surfaces clean

violations.title: Nonfood-Contact Surfaces Kept Clean
violations.observation: The nonfood-contact surfaces of the following equipment had accumulations of grime and debris: many of the refrigerated door handles had dried food encrusted on them. Also, there was a significant amount of food debris inside the front display case which was in need of cleaning
violations.corrective_action: Nonfood-contact surfaces of equipment and utensils shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. Clean the insides of all the refrigerator door handles as soon as possible or before the next routine inspection. They should be cleaned on a regular basis so that food does not accumulate and allow bacteria to grow. Clean the inside of the front display case as soon as possible or before the next routine inspection

violations.title: Physical Facilities, Cleaning Frequency

violations.corrective_action: Clean the physical facilities at a frequency necessary to ensure the protection and safe preparation of food. out_items.name: Food properly labeled, original container

violations.title: Food Storage Container, Common Name

out_items.name: Utensils, equipment and linens properly stored, dried and handled

violations.corrective_action: EHS educated the CFM on proper air drying of utensils, to prevent wet nesting. After cleaning and sanitizing, equipment and utensils shall be air-dried or used after adequate draining before contact with food.

out_items.name: Hot and cold water available, adequate pressure

violations.title: Hot Water Capacity to Meet Peak Demands
violations.observation: After hot water heater calculations, there was a deficiency in hot water generation for the food establishment, per equipment in the facility. Hot water temperatures were adequate at time of inspection, so CFM is given appropriate time for repairs.
violations.corrective_action: The CFM will need to contact Building Department and Health Department, pulling all necessary permits where required, to obtain repairs for the hot water heater to meet the capacity needs of the food establishment.

violations.observation: Floor, floor covering, walls, wall covering, and ceiling is not designed, constructed or installed to be smooth and easily cleanable. EHS observed broken floor tiles in the kitchen area and inside of the walk in cooler.
violations.corrective_action: The CFM will need to repair the floor tiles, making sure that they are smooth and easily cleanable.

violations.title: Physical Facilities, Cleaning Frequency
violations.observation: There was an excessive accumulation of grease, dirt and food debris throughout the food establishment, the floors, walls, and ceilings, under equipment and in corners.
violations.corrective_action: The CFM will need to clean the food establishment to remove the accumulated grease, dirt and food debris throughout the facility. Clean the physical facilities at a frequency necessary to ensure the protection and safe preparation of food.
